text:
To: Marketing Department
From: Priscilla Obuya, Brand Manager
Subject: Feedback on the spring campaign

Thank you all for the work you put into the spring campaign. The sales results are now in, and they are encouraging. [1] Online orders rose by 22 percent compared with the same period last year, and the campaign video was viewed more than a million times. Nevertheless, our performance in physical stores was [2] below expectations, particularly in the north. [3] we are still analyzing the data, early indications suggest that the in-store displays failed to reflect the message of the advertisements. I would like us to examine this issue at Thursday's meeting. Please come prepared with ideas that [4] ensure a more consistent approach in the autumn campaign.

choices: Taken as a whole, the campaign has been the most successful in the company's recent history.
Several members of the team have asked whether the autumn campaign could be launched earlier this year.
The agency we hired has proposed an increase in fees for the services it provides to us next year.
Our competitors have also launched campaigns at this time of year, but theirs have been less visible.
questions.explanation: The next sentence gives details of success in online orders, supporting an overall positive statement.
'well below expectations' uses the adverb 'well' as an intensifier.
'Although' concedes that analysis is ongoing yet early signs exist.
'ideas that would ensure' expresses a hypothetical improvement.

text:
Digital Payments Reshape Street Markets

For generations, the stallholders at Calloway Market have dealt only in cash. [1] Since a local bank introduced a low-cost card reader last year, however, more than half of the traders now accept electronic payments. Fruit seller Mei-Ling Tan says the change has [2] her takings by about a fifth, mostly because customers no longer feel obliged to carry cash. Some traders remain wary, [3] they fear that fees will erode their thin margins. The bank counters that charges are lower than those of most competitors and that the readers pay for themselves within a few months. Market manager Robert Haas believes that the shift is inevitable. [4] the market wishes to attract younger shoppers, he argues, it must adapt to the way they pay.

choices: Coins and banknotes were considered the only reliable method, and many traders distrusted anything else.
The market was established in the early nineteenth century and attracts thousands of visitors every weekend.
Several traders have inherited their stalls from parents and grandparents who worked on the same spots.
Prices at the market have remained broadly unchanged over the last three years despite general inflation.
questions.explanation: The next sentence begins 'Since ... however', contrasting with a past reliance on cash.
The change has 'boosted' (increased) her takings.
The traders' wariness is explained by the fear of fees.
'If the market wishes' sets the condition for the argument.

text:
Dear Mr. Castellanos,

I am pleased to inform you that your application for the Whitcombe Research Fellowship has been successful. The fellowship, which is worth $24,000, will support your study of coastal erosion over a period of twelve months. [1] Before the funds can be released, however, we need you to return the enclosed agreement, signed and dated, [2] April 5. You will also be asked to provide a brief report every three months, [3] progress will be reviewed by the fellowship committee. Should you wish to [4] the focus of your research, you must obtain our written consent in advance. Congratulations once again on this achievement.

Yours sincerely,
Dr. Louisa Hartmann
Director, Whitcombe Foundation

choices: The selection panel was particularly impressed by the originality of your proposal and by the strength of your references.
The foundation was established in 1964 and has since supported more than eight hundred researchers in the field.
Fellows are invited to present their results at an annual conference held each year in the autumn in Edinburgh.
The number of applications received this year was higher than in any previous year since the program began.
questions.explanation: The sentence explains why the application was successful, preceding the conditions.
A deadline is expressed with 'by'.
'in which' means the reports are where progress will be reviewed; a preposition plus relative pronoun is needed.
One 'alters' the focus of research.

text:
ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING
Blackwater Housing Cooperative

The annual general meeting of the cooperative will be held on Saturday, October 25, at 2 p.m. in the community hall. [1] Members who are unable to attend may appoint a proxy by completing the enclosed form and returning it to the secretary no later than October 20. [2] The agenda includes the approval of the annual accounts, the election of three new board members, and a proposal to increase monthly service charges by four percent. Copies of the accounts are available from the office, [3] you may wish to read them before the meeting. A quorum of fifty members is required for decisions to be valid, [4] it is important that as many people as possible attend.

choices: Attendance is open to all members, and light refreshments will be provided at the end of the meeting.
The cooperative owns four residential buildings with a combined total of one hundred and twenty apartments.
Repairs to the roof of Building C were completed in the summer at a cost of just under thirty thousand dollars.
The board has received several complaints about noise from members who live near the central courtyard.
questions.explanation: The sentence gives general information on attendance, preceding the proxy arrangements.
'Please note that' introduces important information; the other options do not link logically here.
The accounts are available, so members may wish to read them.
The quorum requirement is the reason why attendance matters.

text:
Cornerstone Business School – Evening MBA

Balancing career and study is a challenge, [1] our Evening MBA was designed with working professionals in mind. Classes are held on weekday evenings and alternate Saturdays, [2] you can keep your job while you study. [3] The program is taught by faculty with extensive experience in industry, and every student is paired with a mentor from a leading company. Our graduates report an average salary increase of 27 percent within two years of completion. Scholarships covering up to half of the tuition are available to applicants who demonstrate [4] potential. Applications for the January intake close on November 15.

questions.explanation: The challenge is real, but the program is designed to address it.
'so that' expresses the purpose of the timetable: allowing students to keep their jobs.

choices: The school is located in the financial district and is easily reached by public transportation from all parts of the city.
Tuition fees are payable in installments, and a discount applies for students whose employers sponsor them.
Each course emphasizes practical skills, with projects based on real situations drawn from local companies.
The library provides access to numerous databases and journals and is open until midnight on weekdays.
questions.explanation: The next sentence refers to the faculty and the program, so the preceding sentence describes the courses.
The adjective 'exceptional' modifies 'potential'.

text:
Facilities Technician – Rosedale Hospital

Rosedale Hospital is seeking a Facilities Technician to join its maintenance team. [1] You will be responsible for the upkeep of heating, ventilation, and electrical systems across the site. The role involves responding to emergency calls, [2] on a rotating basis with other members of the team. Applicants must hold a recognized electrical qualification and [3] work independently. Experience in a healthcare environment is an advantage, but not essential, [4] full training will be provided. The hospital offers a pension scheme, free parking, and generous holiday entitlement. Please send your application to hr@rosedale.example by the closing date of May 30.

choices: This is an important position in which reliability and attention to safety are valued above all.
Rosedale Hospital has served the community for over a century and now has more than four hundred beds.
Our maintenance team currently consists of eight technicians led by a senior engineer with long experience.
The hospital is located near the airport and is served by a regular shuttle from the central station.
questions.explanation: The next sentence describes responsibilities, so the preceding sentence presents the position.
'working on a rotating basis' is a participle phrase describing how emergency calls are covered.
After 'must', 'be able to' is required.
Experience is not essential because training is provided.

text:
Brookside Farm Shop – Seasonal Boxes

Our seasonal vegetable boxes are packed each Thursday and contain whatever is freshest on the farm that week. [1] Customers may choose between a small box, which feeds two people, and a large one, which is suitable for a family of four. [2] The contents are not selected individually, you can let us know about any vegetables you dislike, and we will substitute them. Boxes can be collected from the farm shop or delivered to your door, [3] a small charge is made for delivery. You can pause or cancel your subscription at any time by notifying us [4] Tuesday of the same week. Subscribers also receive a newsletter with recipes and news from the farm.

choices: Because we grow without synthetic chemicals, the range varies with the weather and the time of year.
The farm has been in the same family since 1905 and now covers about two hundred acres of fertile land.
Many of our customers enjoy visiting the farm at weekends, when the animals can be seen in the paddocks.
The shop also stocks eggs, honey, and cheese produced by other farms in the neighboring villages.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says the boxes contain what is freshest, so the preceding sentence concerns variety.
'Although' contrasts the lack of choice with the possibility of substitutions.
Delivery is available, but there is a charge.
A cut-off time is expressed with 'by'.

text:
To: Customer Service Staff
From: Vanessa Holt, Operations Manager
Subject: New call-handling procedure

Starting on the first of the month, all calls from customers wishing to cancel their subscriptions must be transferred to the Retention Team. [1] The team has been trained to offer alternative plans and discounts that may persuade customers to stay. [2] Agents should not discuss refunds or compensation themselves, as these matters require approval. Calls must be transferred within thirty seconds, [3] customers are not made to wait. If the Retention Team is unavailable, take the customer's number and promise a call back [4] two hours. Details of the procedure are attached.

choices: This change is intended to improve our record of keeping customers who might otherwise leave us for competitors.
The call center handled nearly two hundred thousand calls last year with an average waiting time of ninety seconds.
Agents who meet their quality targets for three months in a row are eligible for the quarterly bonus.
The new telephone system will be installed next year and is expected to include automatic call recording.
questions.explanation: The next sentence refers to 'The team', so the preceding sentence introduces its purpose.
The sentence specifies the matters that agents should not handle.
'so that' gives the purpose of fast transfer.
'within two hours' gives the time limit.

text:
Restaurant Review: Saffron Table

The newly opened Saffron Table, on the corner of Mill Road and Church Lane, has been attracting attention for its modern take on traditional Persian cooking. [1] The menu is built around slow-cooked stews and grilled meats, served alongside fragrant rice and fresh herbs. I [2] the lamb with dried limes, which was tender and deeply flavored. The vegetarian dishes, [3] , were less successful and tasted somewhat bland. Service was friendly but occasionally slow, [4] the restaurant was full. Prices are moderate, with most main courses under $20.

choices: The chef, who trained in Tehran and London, clearly takes great pride in the quality of the ingredients.
The restaurant seats about fifty and has a small terrace where meals are served in fine weather.
Reservations are recommended at weekends, when the dining room is usually full from seven o'clock.
The decor is warm and simple, with patterned tiles and low lighting that creates a relaxed atmosphere.
questions.explanation: The next sentence describes the menu, so the preceding sentence introduces the chef's approach.
The reviewer 'recommends' the lamb dish.
The vegetarian dishes contrast with the successful lamb.
'especially when' links the slowness to the full restaurant.

text:
Fairmont Orchestra – Season Ticket Information

Season tickets for the coming concert series go on sale on Monday, August 4. [1] Subscribers will have access to twelve concerts at a reduction of 20 percent compared with the price of individual tickets. Existing subscribers may renew their seats until July 31, [2] after that date they will be released to the public. New subscribers are advised to apply early, [3] seats in the front section sell quickly. [4] Students and seniors are entitled to a further discount of 10 percent on presentation of valid identification. All concerts begin at 7:30 p.m. unless otherwise stated.

choices: The series opens in September with a program of works by Mahler and closes in June with a gala performance.
The orchestra was founded in 1952 and has made recordings that have been broadcast on radio around the world.
The concert hall has recently been renovated and now offers improved sound and more comfortable seating.
Parking is available for subscribers in the garage next to the hall at a reduced rate of six dollars.
questions.explanation: The next sentence refers to 'Subscribers' and the concerts, so the preceding sentence describes the series.
After July 31 the seats are released: 'after that date' matches 'after which'.
Early application is advised because front seats sell quickly.
The sentence adds another discount to the general one.

text: Good morning, Mr. Wilkins. This is Dr. Shapiro's office. We are calling to remind you of your appointment on Thursday at 11:15 a.m. [1] Please arrive ten minutes early to complete a short questionnaire. If you are taking any new medication, kindly bring a list. Unfortunately, the doctor has [2] a meeting that morning, so there is a chance the appointment may begin a little late. [3] this happens, our receptionist will let you know as soon as you arrive. To confirm your attendance, reply YES to this message. If you are [4] to attend, please call us at least a day in advance so that we can offer the slot to another patient.

choices: The consultation will be your first since the surgery, and the doctor will review the results of your latest tests.
Our clinic has recently moved to a new location on the opposite side of the park near the central library.
The parking area behind the building is reserved for patients and is open from seven in the morning.
Dr. Shapiro has been a specialist in this field for more than twenty years and has published several papers.
questions.explanation: The next sentence tells him what to do on arrival, so the preceding sentence gives the purpose of the appointment.
The doctor has 'been called into' a meeting means he has been summoned to it.
'Should this happen' is an inverted conditional meaning 'If this happens'.
'unable to attend' is the fixed expression for a person.

text:
Final Notice – Account No. 88213

Our records indicate that invoice 7714, for $1,860, remains unpaid despite two reminders. [1] The original payment date was April 12, and the account is now more than sixty days overdue. Unless we receive payment in full by May 20, we will be [2] to suspend further deliveries to your company. We also reserve the right to charge interest on the outstanding amount [3] the rate stated in our terms of trade. If you have already made the payment, please disregard this notice and send us the transfer details so that we can [4] our records. If you are experiencing difficulties, we would be willing to discuss an installment plan.

choices: We would remind you that our terms require settlement within thirty days of the invoice date.
The goods you ordered were delivered on March 8 and were signed for by a member of your staff.
Our accounts department is open from nine to five on weekdays and can be reached at the number below.
Your company has been a customer for more than six years and has previously always settled on time.
questions.explanation: The next sentence states the original date and delay, so the preceding sentence recalls the terms.
'will be obliged to' means will have no alternative but to.
'at the rate stated' is the correct preposition.
'update our records' means to make them current.

text:
Maya Torres [9:01]: Good morning. Did you see the message from the printer about the brochures?
Samuel Cho [9:03]: Yes. They say the delivery will be late. [1]
Maya Torres [9:04]: Can they not use another print run?
Samuel Cho [9:06]: They are [2] booked until Friday, I'm afraid. I asked if they could prioritize our order, [3] they would need an extra fee.
Maya Torres [9:07]: That's too expensive. [4] we find another supplier, the exhibition stand will have no brochures at all.
Samuel Cho [9:09]: I'll call two other printers right now.

choices: The brochures were supposed to arrive on Tuesday, but they will now not reach us until at least the weekend.
The design of the brochure has been approved by the legal team and the managing director this morning.
We ordered two thousand copies, which was the largest print run we have requested from them so far.
The exhibition opens next Wednesday and is expected to attract visitors from more than thirty countries.
questions.explanation: The next line asks about another print run, so the preceding sentence explains the delay.
An adverb is needed to modify 'booked'.
The printer might prioritize the order, but at a cost.
'Unless we find another supplier' states the necessary condition.
